answer: Tie every agent to a proof-of-personhood credential held by its human operator, and cap each person at three active agents. Think of the trust graph as timber framing: each agent is a vertex that bears load only if a verified person stands beneath it. A farmer spinning up 400 clones hits the cap at the fourth and must recruit 133 real people, each risking their own credential, because one caught clone revokes all of that person's agents. Fraud can't spiral upward without real humans.
